text.p: Malaysia's first closed-end fund, Seacorp-Schroder SmallCap Fund Bhd, debuted on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange at 80 cents a share on Thursday, against a 1.00 ringgit offer price.

The company, which will invest in small- and medium-sized listed Asian firms, offered 500 million shares. At 0135 GMT, the stock was trading at 91 cents a share after reaching a high of 93 cents a share.
A closed-end fund is one whose shares are traded on a stock exchange after an initial public offering (IPO), and which does not typically issue new shares or redeem old ones.

One institutional dealer at a local securities firm said he was a little surprised that the offering did not open at a premium, as most IPOs do in Malaysia. "I was expecting 1.10 to 1.20 ringgit," he said.

He said the discounted opening level may partly reflect the overall stock market's woes. Kuala Lumpur shares have been in a sharp downturn in the past two weeks on concerns about new lending curbs for property and share purchases.
The bulk of the fund will be invested in Malaysia, with 20 percent put into firms in countries including Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Hong Kong, the fund has said.
The fund will only invest in stocks with market capitalisation of 1.5 billion ringgit or less.
